title: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman returns to independent Bangladesh
detail: After release from Pakistani custody, Mujib returned and became the central political authority of the postwar state, turning wartime legitimacy into domestic government.

title: Parliamentary government begins under a provisional constitutional order
detail: The new state shifted from wartime proclamation to a parliamentary framework, with a cabinet system and a search for stable civilian institutions after liberation.

title: Constituent Assembly begins work and forms a drafting committee
detail: The Constituent Assembly first met on 10 April, and on the following day formed a 34-member Constitution Drafting Committee chaired by Dr Kamal Hossain.

title: Constitution is adopted
detail: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, setting out parliamentary government, fundamental rights, and the state principles of nationalism, socialism, democracy, and secularism.

title: Constitution takes effect on Victory Day
detail: The constitution came into force on the first anniversary of victory, symbolically binding the memory of liberation to the legal order of the new republic.
